translations.text: And in all Israel there was no man as praised for his beauty as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head there was no blemish in him at all.

And when he cut the hair of his head: from the beginning of the year until that time he would not cut his hair, because it grew heavy on him. When he cut the hair of his head, it weighed a hundred shekels by the royal weight.
And Absalom had three sons and one daughter. The daughter's name was Maacah, and she was very beautiful. Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, took her as his wife, and she bore Abijah.
And Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two whole years and did not see the king's face.
Absalom called Joab to him so that he could send him to the king, but Joab would not come to him. Then he sent a second time, and he still would not come to him.

Then Absalom said to his servants: "Look now, see: isn't Joab's plot near our estate? He has a [?] there sown with barley, [?ripe]. Go now, see to it, and burn it!" So Absalom's servants went and burned Joab's plot. And Joab's servants came with their garments torn and said to him: "Absalom's servants have burned the plot of our cultivated field."
And Joab got up at once, went to Absalom, and said to him: "Why have your servants burned the plot of my estate with fire?"

And Absalom said to Joab: "I sent to you once and said: 'Come to me, and I will send you to the king so that you can say to him: Why did I come from Geshur? I have come and I sit here. It would have been better for me to be there than to come and sit here without seeing the king's face. If there is any wickedness in me, put me to death!'"

And Joab went to the king and told him all these words. And the king ordered Absalom to be brought. He came in before the king and bowed down with his face to the ground. And the king called Absalom to him, embraced him, and kissed him on the face.
And after this Absalom began to acquire chariots and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before his chariots and horses.

And Absalom would rise early in the morning and come and stand by the road in front of the gates. Whenever a man had a case against his neighbour and was coming to the king for judgment, Absalom would call him over and ask him: "Where do you come from, and what city are you from?" And the man would tell him what lineage he was from: "Your servant is from the tribes of Israel."
Absalom would answer and say to him: "Look, your words are good and right, but there is no one before the king to hear what you would see fit to plead."
And then Absalom would say: "If only someone would appoint me ruler and judge over Israel [?]! Then every man who came to me for judgment, I would judge him with righteous judgment."
And whenever any man came near to bow down to him, he would put out his hand, draw him close, and kiss him on the face.
Absalom did this every day to every Israelite who came before the king for judgment. In this way Absalom won over the hearts of all the men of Israel.
And after the fourth year Absalom began to speak to the king and said to him: "Let me go and fulfil my vow, which I vowed to the Lord God in Hebron."
